s-a932b67bc7.title: NIH 2009 stem-cell guidelines
s-a932b67bc7.finding: New framework effective 7 July 2009; eligible hESC research permitted subject to law. Not removal of every embryo-research funding restriction.

s-09929e2f31.title: NIH new hESC registry approvals paused
s-09929e2f31.finding: Pause on review/approval of new hESC registry lines; existing registered lines remain usable. Embryo derivation funding remains prohibited.

s-2c776a61a6.title: NIH stem-cell FAQs
s-2c776a61a6.finding: Current FAQ repeats the new hESC registry review/approval pause.

s-f46c49ef91.title: Second summit organising-committee statement
s-f46c49ef91.finding: Condemns the reported edited-births procedure; reiterates opposition to current germline clinical use and calls for standards. Nonbinding, not a UK law amendment.

s-35af88b0f4.title: CDC response to anthrax and influenza incidents
s-35af88b0f4.finding: 11 July transfer moratorium and working group; action followed both anthrax and H5N1 incidents. Some reforms underway/planned.

s-1a41fcc7f3.title: CDC Director testimony
s-1a41fcc7f3.finding: Transfer moratorium lifted lab-by-lab after corrective action; agency policy, not a worldwide ban.

s-837bd42dc9.title: First CDC laboratory resumes specified transfers
s-837bd42dc9.finding: 24 July first specified TB-lab transfer permission; not a universal end date.

s-eada04f7e1.title: HFEA embryo-editing research licence
s-eada04f7e1.finding: Research licence approved subject to ethics approval; research embryos cannot be transferred for treatment.

s-40589e1f99.title: MRC genome editing policy
s-40589e1f99.finding: Distinguishes licensed germline laboratory research and supported somatic clinical work from prohibited heritable clinical applications. Updated 13 February 2026.

s-hfe-original-treatment.title: HFE Act 1990, original Schedule 2 paragraph 1(4)
s-hfe-original-treatment.finding: Treatment licences could not authorise alteration of the genetic structure of a cell forming part of an embryo. Research licences were separately governed.

s-hfe-schedule-commencement.title: HFE Act Schedule 2: commencement and amended treatment provisions
s-hfe-schedule-commencement.review_depth: Selected statutory provisions and commencement annotation
s-hfe-schedule-commencement.finding: Schedule 2 wholly in force on 1 August 1991. Later wording includes the specific permitted mitochondrial-donation exception.

s-ipsc-applications.title: NIH induced pluripotent stem cell research overview
s-ipsc-applications.review_depth: Substantive overview text in indexed result
s-ipsc-applications.finding: Reprogrammed somatic cells supply pluripotent cells for disease research and drug discovery. The chart note synthesises this alternative source with the original human-iPSC milestone; it does not quantify substitution or imply complete replacement of hESCs.

Stem-cell research.subtitle: Red: US hESC line eligibility
Stem-cell research.explanation: The overview red periods concern NIH hESC line eligibility: the 2001 restriction was replaced in July 2009; a distinct pause on new registry approvals began in January 2026. Dickey–Wicker remains in the evidence table, but is not used to colour the entire stem-cell/iPSC narrative. iPSCs are a non-embryonic alternative, not the target of the hESC eligibility limit.

CRISPR / heritable editing.subtitle: Red: reproductive genome editing
CRISPR / heritable editing.explanation: Red begins with the August 1991 treatment-licence restriction on genetic alteration of embryo cells and continues under the amended framework from October 2009. This is not a blanket ban on CRISPR research. Licensed research and the specific mitochondrial-donation exception are distinct; the summit statement did not change UK law.

Stem-cell research.subjects: NIH review and approval of new hESC registry lines. Already approved lines remain eligible; not an iPSC ban or all-hESC ban.
Stem-cell research.activities: Review and approval of new hESC registry lines.
Stem-cell research.continuation_basis: January notice and current NIH FAQ describe the pause. No verified lifting date found.

CRISPR / heritable editing.short_label: Embryo genetic alteration excluded from treatment licences [UK]
CRISPR / heritable editing.subjects: UK treatment licences: genetic alteration of a cell while it forms part of an embryo. Not a statement about all research or pre-1991 law.
CRISPR / heritable editing.continuation_basis: Original Schedule 2 paragraph 1(4) applied from August 1991. Replaced by amended provisions in October 2009; the separately mapped successor restriction continues.

findings.text: The edited-births claim was discussed at the already organised 2018 summit. Its statement was a nonbinding response, not an immediate UK law change.
The 11 July 2014 transfer moratorium was an implemented agency action following two incidents. Resumption was lab-specific, so no whole-field red interval with a guessed endpoint is added.
2009 widened hESC eligibility; embryo-derivation funding restrictions persisted. January 2026 added a distinct new-line registry pause. None is a blanket iPSC ban.
Research and reproductive applications have different rules. The red label now names reproductive use.
Human iPSCs provide a non-embryonic pluripotent-cell source for many research applications. This can reduce reliance on hESCs, but is not universal equivalence or replacement of all embryo research.
